lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Digital Life, Purchases, and Consumer Skills
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: returns and warranties

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic returns and warranties task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner locates one real receipt, product box, or warranty document already present in the household and reads it closely to find the exact return window and what the warranty does and does not cover.

simulationAlternative.description: If no receipt, box, or warranty document is available in the household, the learner instead reads a provided sample receipt and warranty document and answers the same questions using that sample.

materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific detail in this document you would have missed if you had only skimmed it, and why reading the exact terms matters before assuming something is or is not covered.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Term identification accuracy: The exact return window and at least two specific coverage or exclusion terms are correctly found. | Applied reasoning: A specific warranty or return term is correctly cited to support whether the item would be covered. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner compare the warranty terms on two different real (or sample) products and identify which one offers stronger consumer protection and why.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic returns and warranties task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: returns and warranties worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner locates one real receipt, product box, or warranty document already present in the household and reads it closely to find the exact return window and what the warranty does and does not cover.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact returns and warranties decision or action.
Model move 2: Find one real receipt, product box, or warranty document already in the household.
Model move 3: Read the document closely and find the exact return window (how many days) and the specific conditions the warranty covers or excludes.

Model check: Term identification accuracy: The exact return window and at least two specific coverage or exclusion terms are correctly found. | Applied reasoning: A specific warranty or return term is correctly cited to support whether the item would be covered.

resources.title: returns and warranties action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for returns and warranties.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: returns and warranties coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner locates one real receipt, product box, or warranty document already present in the household and reads it closely to find the exact return window and what the warranty does and does not cover.
Coach direction: Find one real receipt, product box, or warranty document already in the household.
Learner prompt: Name the item and where you found the document: on a receipt, on the box, or on separate warranty paper.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: returns and warranties complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Read the document closely and find the exact return window (how many days) and the specific conditions the warranty covers or excludes.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I found the exact number of days in the return window, not an estimate.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I found at least two specific things the warranty covers and at least one thing it excludes.

Equal-access rule: If no receipt, box, or warranty document is available in the household, the learner instead reads a provided sample receipt and warranty document and answers the same questions using that sample.

resources.title: returns and warranties minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one specific detail in this document you would have missed if you had only skimmed it, and why reading the exact terms matters before assuming something is or is not covered.

Success checks: Term identification accuracy: The exact return window and at least two specific coverage or exclusion terms are correctly found. | Applied reasoning: A specific warranty or return term is correctly cited to support whether the item would be covered.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: returns and warranties supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional returns and warranties condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Term identification accuracy: The exact return window and at least two specific coverage or exclusion terms are correctly found. | Applied reasoning: A specific warranty or return term is correctly cited to support whether the item would be covered..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

resources.title: returns and warranties delivered sample
resources.purpose: Resolves the lesson's named sample so the learner is never directed to a phantom material.

Field 1 (t2-p1): I found the exact number of days in the return window, not an estimate.
Field 2 (t2-p2): I found at least two specific things the warranty covers and at least one thing it excludes.

Check against: Term identification accuracy: The exact return window and at least two specific coverage or exclusion terms are correctly found. | Applied reasoning: A specific warranty or return term is correctly cited to support whether the item would be covered.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner locates one real receipt, product box, or warranty document already present in the household and reads it closely to find the exact return window and what the warranty does and does not cover.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Name the item and where you found the document: on a receipt, on the box, or on separate warranty paper.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Term identification accuracy: The exact return window and at least two specific coverage or exclusion terms are correctly found.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

realRoute.title: returns and warranties — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Read the document closely and find the exact return window (how many days) and the specific conditions the warranty covers or excludes.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: returns and warranties — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: If no receipt, box, or warranty document is available in the household, the learner instead reads a provided sample receipt and warranty document and answers the same questions using that sample.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain one specific detail in this document you would have missed if you had only skimmed it, and why reading the exact terms matters before assuming something is or is not covered.
observableCriteria: Term identification accuracy: The exact return window and at least two specific coverage or exclusion terms are correctly found.
Applied reasoning: A specific warranty or return term is correctly cited to support whether the item would be covered.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Term identification accuracy: The exact return window and at least two specific coverage or exclusion terms are correctly found. | Applied reasoning: A specific warranty or return term is correctly cited to support whether the item would be covered.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
